name: Sustainable Smart Farm
description: Immersive VR training in which a learner inspects a farm, collects soil and water samples, performs chemical analysis, identifies soil/water/crop issues, chooses a sustainable agricultural action and observes its environmental impact.

ontologies.focus: chemical testing of soil, water and fertilizer

Scene.query: farm agricultural field cropland plot orchard paddy greenhouse watershed ecosystem soil water body environment
Scene.guidance: the farm as the spatial container; the specific fields/plots, water bodies (well, canal, stream, groundwater) and the field laboratory where analysis happens.

Article.query: soil sample water sample crop plant pest organism fertilizer agrochemical implement equipment instrument sensor reagent
Article.guidance: Tangible in-scene objects: soil and water samples, sampling tools, test instruments and reagents, crops, pests, agricultural inputs (fertilizer, amendments, mulch) and the learner.

ActionResponse.query: sampling process chemical analysis measurement method fertilizer application irrigation tillage pest control environmental process response
ActionResponse.guidance: One stereotype per user interaction with its system response: field inspection, soil/water sampling, each chemical analysis method, applying an agricultural action, observing the impact.

Behavior.query: soil quality threshold limit salinity acidity nutrient balance contamination degradation erosion compaction condition rule
Behavior.guidance: Rules, not processes: name them as limits/rules (…Threshold, …Limit, …Rule, …Quota, …Safeguard). Soil/water quality thresholds, diagnosis rules that identify an issue, admissibility of agricultural actions, water quotas and environmental safeguards from the SOPs.

Timeline.query: cropping season crop rotation growth stage schedule sequence of farming operations monitoring cycle protocol
Timeline.guidance: Ordered sequences, not single processes: the VR training session as ordered phases; its step/phase stereotype, the cropping season or rotation cycle, and the post-action monitoring schedule.
